camps.name: Perfect Pass
camps.why: The standard high camp: benches beside the Challenger Glacier put the summit within a short day, and you sleep there before and after it. Windy, and snow-covered early in the season.

camps.name: Copper Creek camp
camps.why: A low trail camp with water and a toilet, used as a first-night stop on a slower five-day trip or as the retreat if the Chilliwack ford looks bad.

camps.name: Whatcom Pass camp
camps.why: Belongs to the Brush Creek approach rather than Easy Ridge. Parties who come in over Whatcom Pass sleep here, then get around Whatcom Peak to reach Perfect Pass.

new_camps.name: Easy Ridge crest camp
new_camps.why: Where the long first day ends: past the Chilliwack ford and the steep climb, with ridge views and a tarn nearby. It splits the Perfect Pass approach into two manageable days.
new_camps.water: A tarn lies near the crest.
new_camps.notes: Elevation is approximate, taken from a party that camped just short of the 6,553 ft point on the crest. Tent sites are scattered along the ridge, with more on Easy Peak.

camps.name: Perfect Pass, Perfect Pass cross-country zone
camps.why: The staging camp for Challenger and the Pinnacle: benches at the edge of the glacier, so summit day starts a few hundred yards from the tent.

camps.name: Challenger Arm camp
camps.why: Reached from the Wiley Ridge side, so it is not slept at on the Hannegan Pass plan. It is slightly closer to the Pinnacle but on the wrong approach.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: Belongs to the Ross Lake side of the Pickets and is not on the Hannegan Pass line, so it is not used on this plan.

camps.name: Beaver Pass Camp
camps.why: Big camp for the Wiley Ridge route from Ross Lake. It would add days to this plan, so parties coming from Hannegan Pass skip it.

camps.name: Eiley Lake benches, lower Wiley Ridge
camps.why: First bivouac ground on the Wiley Ridge approach from the east. Not on this plan, which comes in via Easy Ridge.

camps.name: East Wiley Basin and the Wiley Lake benches, upper Wiley Ridge
camps.why: Last bivouac ground before the glacier on the Wiley Ridge approach. Not used on a Hannegan Pass trip.

plan_conflict: The plan reaches Perfect Pass on day 1 (16 miles, 7,000 ft), but most parties report breaking the approach with a night on Easy Ridge; the Challenger Arm camp on file is a Wiley Ridge camp, not a main for this plan.

camps.name: Access Creek Basin
camps.why: First stop above the Access Creek bushwhack, with creek water and the long scree chute to Access Col still ahead. Most parties arrive tired in the evening.

camps.name: Luna Col (Luna Pass)
camps.why: High camp for Fury. Cuts the summit day approach and has a snowfield for water, but flat ground is scarce and the saddle is windy.

new_camps.name: Access Creek Basin
new_camps.why: Where the Access Creek bushwhack ends; creek water here, and it leaves a bearable climb to Access Col the next morning.
new_camps.notes: Elevation as shown on the app's own map pin for this basin.

new_camps.name: Luna Col (Luna Pass)
new_camps.why: Gets you over Access Col and back to a camp near the ridge after the climb. Windy, with little flat ground, but a snowfield can supply water.
new_camps.water: A small snowfield at the saddle normally runs water.
new_camps.notes: Elevation as shown on the app's own map pin. Some parties bivouac high on the mountain instead of returning on night 4.

new_camps.name: Luna Cirque camp
new_camps.why: Puts you directly under the North Buttress for a pre-dawn start, at the cost of a 2,400 ft descent and re-climb to Luna Col.
new_camps.water: A creek about eight minutes west of the camp.
new_camps.notes: Elevation is approximate, from a party that camped in the cirque below the buttress.

plan_conflict: No camps are on file for this route; night 4 at Luna Col is the plan's assumption and the plan itself allows a high bivouac, which was not confirmed by any party's report.

camps.name: Access Basin
camps.why: The usual first night: the bushwhack is behind you, water is at hand, and Access Col is a morning's climb away.

camps.name: Luna Col (Luna Pass)
camps.why: Closest camp to the Southeast Glacier, so summit day is a round trip from the tent. Windy and short of flat sites, with a snowfield for water.

camps.name: Luna Camp
camps.why: A trail camp nine miles up Big Beaver. Slower parties, or those starting from the landing late, stop here before the Access Creek bushwhack the next day.

plan_conflict: Luna Camp and Access Basin are both on file as main; only Access Basin is slept at on night 1 of this plan, so Luna Camp is changed to route.

camps.name: Access Creek headwaters basin
camps.why: Open basin above the bushwhack; the usual first night before Access Col, with creek water.

camps.name: East Fury summit bivy
camps.why: Flat rock on East Fury that sits at the jumping-off point for the ridge, and where a bivy sack can be left standing for the return.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: Trail camp short of the Access Creek bushwhack. Parties wanting an easier first day stop here, which adds a long day to reach East Fury.

camps.name: Luna Col bivy, Luna cross-country zone
camps.why: The place parties sleep after the summit and the connecting ridge, before the long exit; a snowfield can supply water, but flat ground is scarce.

new_camps.name: Mongo Ridge open bivy
new_camps.why: There are no real sites on the ridge; parties sleep on the towers or in the moat of a small glacier above the Pole of Remoteness, with a sit pad and bag.
new_camps.notes: Bivies have been taken on Tower 1, Tower 3 and a high bivy near False Fury. No elevation found for any of them.

plan_conflict: The plan's nights 3 and 4 are on the ridge itself; no ridge bivy has a researched elevation, and Luna Col bivy is changed from route to main for night 5.

camps.name: Luna Col bivy, Luna cross-country zone
camps.why: The working high camp for both Furies: a snowfield for water and the traverse starts from the tent, but expect wind and very little flat ground.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: Trail camp at the start of the Access Creek bushwhack. A party splitting the 18-mile first day stops here, but that adds a day to this 3-day plan.

camps.name: Luna Cirque floor
camps.why: Low bivy under Luna Peak, used by parties traversing the range rather than by a Fury round trip out of Luna Col.

plan_conflict: Luna Camp is on file as main; a party doing this 3-day plan reaches Luna Col on day 1, so Luna Camp is changed to route.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: A flat old-growth camp nine miles up the Big Beaver trail, a gentle first day that leaves the bushwhack and Access Col for the next.

camps.name: Luna Col bivy, Luna cross-country zone
camps.why: High camp for the traverse day: a snowfield gives water and the ridge starts here, though flat ground is scarce and the saddle takes wind.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: Flat trail camp on Big Beaver, the first night in and the last before the exit; it saves a day of bushwhacking on the way back.

camps.name: Luna Cirque floor
camps.why: The bowl under the glacier: shelter on three sides and water, and the shortest way to the route. Parties may pitch an advance camp higher on the moraine.

plan_conflict: The plan calls for a separate advance camp below the icefall on nights 3 and 4, but no camp or pin exists for it and no report was found, so the cirque floor is assumed to cover those nights.

camps.name: Whatcom Camp, Brush Creek below Whatcom Pass
camps.why: Nearest established camp under the pass, so day 2 starts on the glacier. The plan says it may be closed, in which case sleep in the zone above the pass.

camps.name: Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine high camp
camps.why: Closest camp to Phantom: the summit day is a round trip from here. It is a moraine bivouac with water from melt, and you cross two glaciers to reach it.

camps.name: Luna Cirque floor
camps.why: Belongs to the Ross Lake side. A party doing the Pickets traverse might sleep here, but the Hannegan Pass plan never does.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: Ross Lake side trail camp. It is not on the Hannegan Pass plan and only matters to parties coming from Big Beaver.

camps.name: Perfect Pass, Perfect Pass cross-country zone
camps.why: A strong camp on the way past the Challenger Glacier. Parties with an earlier start or a shorter day 1 could sleep here instead of Whatcom Pass.

plan_conflict: The camps on file include Luna Cirque floor as main, but the plan sleeps above Whatcom Pass and at a Crooked Thumb moraine; Whatcom Camp is used for nights 1 and 4 only as an assumption.

camps.name: Easy Ridge bivouac ground below Easy Peak
camps.why: Where the steep climb out of the Chilliwack ends, with views and a tarn; it splits the long approach and puts the Impasse next in the morning.

camps.name: Perfect Pass, Perfect Pass cross-country zone
camps.why: The standard base for the Pinnacle: sleep next to the glacier, climb with a light pack, and return to the same tent for the second night.

camps.name: Easy Ridge bivouac ground below Easy Peak
camps.why: The first-night stop past Easy Peak, where the long ridge day ends and the climbers' path gives way to the Impasse.

camps.name: Improvised bivouacs on the Challenger Glacier and the crest south of Challenger
camps.why: No established site exists near Spectre: parties bivy on moraine or ice south of Challenger and use it before and after the climb.

camps.name: Perfect Pass, Perfect Pass cross-country zone
camps.why: A better-sheltered camp with real benches, but about 4 miles farther from the climb than the bivy near Spectre. Parties wanting comfort sleep here.

plan_conflict: The plan's day 4 starts with the descent, so night 3 is spent at the approach bivy (or on the descent), not at the car; the first-night bivy beyond Easy Peak is the Easy Ridge ground on file.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: The first night on the Ross Lake approach: flat, forested, and close enough to the Access Creek bushwhack to start fresh.

camps.name: Luna Col bivy, Luna cross-country zone
camps.why: High camp after Access Col, with snowfield water and the Fury traverse starting next; flat space is scarce and it is windy.

camps.name: Luna Cirque floor
camps.why: Lower alternative on the traverse that skips the col; it adds a descent and re-climb, so most parties sleep at Luna Col.

new_camps.name: Glacier col bivy past West Fury
new_camps.why: After the Fury traverse parties have been seen camping on snow in a wind hollow at a glacier col before Swiss; there is no real site.
new_camps.notes: Described by one traverse party only. No elevation found.

plan_conflict: The plan gives no camps for days 3 and 4; night 3 is taken from a single traverse account and the plan's day 1 names both Luna Camp and Access Creek.

new_camps.name: Easy Peak bivy
new_camps.why: Where the first day ends on the crest; a tarn is nearby, and it puts the Impasse and Perfect Pass in reach for day 2.
new_camps.water: A tarn on or near the summit.
new_camps.notes: Elevation taken from the app's own pin. Parties also camp lower on Easy Ridge.

new_camps.name: Perfect Pass
new_camps.why: Closest camp to the route: about 45 minutes to the base of the south buttress. Sleep here after the climb rather than walk out the same night.
new_camps.notes: Elevation approximate; reports range from about 6,240 to 6,300 ft. Windy; snow-covered early.

plan_conflict: The plan descends and walks all the way out on day 3, so night 2 at Perfect Pass is an assumption; no report of a Castle in the Sky party's nights was found.

camps.name: Whatcom Camp, Brush Creek below Whatcom Pass
camps.why: Closest camp to the North Ridge: summit day is a short round trip and you return to the same tent. Flat ground has been scarce since washouts.

camps.name: Twin Rocks and Stillwell Camps, Little Beaver
camps.why: Belongs to the Little Beaver approach from the water taxi; useful for a loop with an exit over Beaver Pass, not for the Hannegan Pass plan.

camps.name: Easy Ridge bivouac ground below Easy Peak
camps.why: Ends the first day high on the crest, before the Impasse bypass the next morning; tarn water near the top of the climbers' path.

camps.name: Perfect Pass, Perfect Pass cross-country zone
camps.why: A day of crest and snow brings you to the benches below the south face; on this plan you reach it before the climb and leave it after.

camps.name: Whatcom Camp, Brush Creek below Whatcom Pass
camps.why: Sits on the walk out. Tired parties after the summit may stop here instead of continuing down to US Cabin, saving some distance.

new_camps.name: US Cabin Camp
new_camps.why: Trail camp on the Chilliwack River, about 2 miles past Copper Creek, reached by cable car; a gentler last night with a shorter exit.
new_camps.permit: A North Cascades backcountry permit is required.
new_camps.notes: Hiker and stock camps. No elevation found.

plan_conflict: The plan sleeps night 3 at US Cabin Camp, which is not on file; the plan's route there is not a report any party was found to have followed.

camps.name: Terror Basin camp
camps.why: The only mountain camp near the spire: summit day starts near the glacier outlet and returns here before the walk out. Overnights need a park permit.

camps.name: Goodell Creek Campground, roadhead staging
camps.why: Car camping the night before for a pre-dawn start; it advances you not at all, but gives hot water, tables and bear boxes.

camps.name: Old Goodell Creek roadbed near the Terror Creek crossing
camps.why: Fallback for parties starting late: flat-ish ground before the steep climb, but it puts the hardest part of the approach on the next day.
